extraFacts.fact: ASME B16.34 sets pressure-temperature ratings for flanged, threaded and welding-end valves by pressure class (150 to 2500) and material group; the allowable working pressure for a class falls as temperature rises.
extraFacts.source: ASME B16.34 Valves - Flanged, Threaded, and Welding End

faqs.q: What is the cast floating ball valve to ISO 17292 used for?
faqs.a: It is the general-purpose quarter-turn valve for process, utility and tank lines in ASME Class 150 and 300. A cast body carries a floating ball between soft seats that give bubble-tight shut-off, and a quarter turn opens or closes it, with a straight bore for low pressure drop when open.

faqs.q: What sizes and classes does the cast floating ball valve to ISO 17292 come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 1/2" to 10" (DN15 to DN250) in ASME Class 150 and 300, with flanged (RF, FF, RTJ) or butt-weld ends. The size table lists 22 standard size and class combinations with length, height and weight, so you can check the valve against the pipe layout before you enquire.

faqs.q: End-entry or two-piece body: how do I choose the cast floating ball valve?
faqs.a: Pick the one-piece end-entry body where lowest cost and fewest body joints matter, and the two-piece split body where the seats may need replacing in service. An end-entry valve has no joint in the pressure boundary, so it has fewer leak paths. Then fix size, class, body and seat material, end connection and operator.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature range does the cast ISO 17292 floating ball valve cover?
faqs.a: The listing covers ASME Class 150 and 300 in a temperature range of -46 °C to 200 °C. Class ratings follow ASME B16.34, where allowable pressure falls as temperature rises, so the pressure you may use at 200 °C is lower than at ambient. Send the design pressure and temperature and we confirm the class.

faqs.q: What materials are the cast floating ball valve's body and seats made from?
faqs.a: The body is cast carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex, and the soft seats are RPTFE, PTFE or reinforced PTFE. Soft seats give bubble-tight shut-off, with a lower temperature ceiling than metal seats; choose the body for the fluid and the seat for temperature, abrasion and cleanliness.

faqs.q: Which standards and test documents apply to the cast floating ball valve, ISO 17292 type?
faqs.a: The listing gives the design standards as ISO 17292, API 6D and ASME B16.34, fire-safe design to API 607 and API 6FA, and hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D. Each valve comes with material certificates to EN 10204 3.1 and the pressure-test record; low-emission packing to ISO 15848 is available on request.

faqs.q: What operators and end connections can the cast floating ball valve be supplied with?
faqs.a: Ends are RF, FF or RTJ flanged or butt-weld, and operation is by lever, gear operator, or a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator on an ISO 5211 mounting. For automated lines see our [actuated valves](/c/actuated-valves); give us the torque or the actuator you plan to fit when you enquire.

faqs.q: How should the cast floating ball valve be installed and looked after?
faqs.a: Line pressure pushes the ball onto the downstream seat, so fit it with the pipework supported and aligned, and cycle it from time to time so the seats do not stick. The blow-out proof stem and anti-static device are built in. Our [guide to floating and trunnion mounted ball valves](/blog/floating-vs-trunnion-mounted-ball-valves) covers when to move up a design.

faqs.q: Which lines is the cast floating ball valve to ISO 17292 used on?
faqs.a: The listing names process, utility, tank and chemical lines. It is the economical choice for on-off isolation in Class 150 and 300 where tight shut-off is wanted and the fluid is clean enough for soft seats; for abrasive or very hot service use a metal seated type instead.

faqs.q: How does the cast floating ball valve differ from the forged side entry floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The cast valve covers NPS 1/2" to 10" in Class 150 and 300 with end-entry or two-piece body, while the [forged side-entry valve](/p/forged-floating-ball-valve-side-entry) covers NPS 1/2" to 6" in Class 150 to 2500 with a two- or three-piece forged body and PEEK or Devlon seats available. Use the forged valve for higher classes and small sizes.

faqs.q: What is the floating double block and bleed compact ball valve used for?
faqs.a: It puts two isolation valves and a bleed valve in one body, so closing both balls and opening the bleed proves positive isolation for maintenance. It takes less weight and space than two separate valves with a spool and bleed between them, which matters on offshore platforms and ships.

faqs.q: What sizes and classes does the floating double block and bleed ball valve come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 2" to 24" (DN50 to DN600) in ASME Class 150 to 2500, with RF or RTJ flanged ends in a three-piece body, long or short pattern. No size table is held on this listing; the general arrangement drawing with face-to-face lengths is issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: What does double block and bleed mean on the floating DBB compact ball valve?
faqs.a: Two seals close against pressure on one side and the space between them is vented. If the first seal leaks, the bleed shows it and the second seal still holds. This valve builds both balls and the bleed into a single three-piece body instead of two valves with a spool between them.

faqs.q: What pressure class is the floating double block and bleed compact ball valve rated for?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME Class 150 to 2500 with hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D. The class you may use depends on body material and temperature under ASME B16.34, which lowers the allowable pressure as temperature rises. Give us the design pressure and temperature and we confirm the class and material.

faqs.q: What materials is the floating double block and bleed ball valve made from?
faqs.a: The body is offered in carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex. The listing does not name a seat material for this valve, so we confirm seat and ball material against the fluid, temperature and class when you send the data sheet.

faqs.q: Which standards and fire-safe design apply to the floating double block and bleed ball valve?
faqs.a: The listing gives API 6D and ASME B16.34 as design standards, fire-safe design to API 607, and hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D. Material certificates and the pressure-test record are supplied with the valve, and third-party inspection can be added when the order specifies it.

faqs.q: How is the floating double block and bleed ball valve operated and connected?
faqs.a: Ends are RF or RTJ flanged, and each ball can be fitted with a lever, gear operator, or a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator. For automated isolation see our [actuated valves](/c/actuated-valves) and tell us the operator and torque requirement when you enquire.

faqs.q: How is the floating double block and bleed ball valve used for positive isolation?
faqs.a: Close both balls, open the bleed, and check that nothing flows from it; a steady flow shows the upstream seat is leaking, while a dry bleed shows the space is isolated. Treat the bleed outlet as a pressure connection and pipe it to a safe vent or drain.

faqs.q: Where is the floating double block and bleed compact ball valve used?
faqs.a: The listing names offshore, marine, instrument and process isolation. The single-body design suits skids, wellhead and instrument take-offs and ship pipework where space and weight are tight and a proven isolation point is needed for maintenance.

faqs.q: How does the floating double block and bleed ball valve differ from the cast floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The DBB valve combines two balls and a bleed in one body and spans NPS 2" to 24" in Class 150 to 2500, while the [cast floating ball valve](/p/cast-floating-ball-valve-iso-17292) is a single-ball on-off valve with a published size table. Choose the DBB valve when isolation must be proved, not just made.

faqs.q: What is the forged side entry floating ball valve used for?
faqs.a: It is a forged two- or three-piece floating ball valve for the higher pressure classes, an economical alternative to small trunnion mounted valves. The forged body takes Class 1500 and 2500 in the small sizes, with soft seats for tight shut-off on high-pressure process and utility lines.

faqs.q: What sizes and classes does the forged side entry floating ball valve come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 1/2" to 6" (DN15 to DN150) in ASME Class 150 to 2500, with flanged RF or RTJ, butt-weld, socket-weld or NPT ends. The size table holds 24 rows with face-to-face length, height and weight, so check the class and size you need against it.

faqs.q: Which seat material should I choose for the forged side entry ball valve?
faqs.a: PTFE and RPTFE suit Class 150 to 600. For Class 900 and above, PEEK or Devlon seats keep their shape under load. Temperature matters as much as class, so tell us the fluid and the design temperature when you enquire.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature range does the forged floating ball valve cover?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME Class 150 to 2500 and -46 °C to 200 °C. Under ASME B16.34 the allowable pressure for each class falls as temperature rises, and soft seats set a lower ceiling than the body. State the design pressure and temperature and we confirm the class, body and seat.

faqs.q: What is the forged side entry floating ball valve made from?
faqs.a: The body is forged carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex, and the seats are PTFE, RPTFE, PEEK or Devlon. The forged body suits the higher classes; the seat is chosen on pressure and temperature as described under the seat question.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the forged side entry floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The listing gives ISO 17292 and ASME B16.34 as design standards, fire-safe design to API 607 and API 6FA, and hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D. Material certificates and the pressure-test record come with the valve; third-party inspection can be added when the order specifies it.

faqs.q: What end connections and operators suit the forged side entry floating ball valve?
faqs.a: Ends can be RF or RTJ flanged, butt-weld, socket-weld or NPT, and operation is by lever, gear operator, or a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator. For larger or heavier-duty duty compare [trunnion mounted ball valves](/c/trunnion-mounted-ball-valves).

faqs.q: Why choose a two-piece or three-piece forged floating ball valve for maintenance?
faqs.a: A three-piece body lets the centre section, with ball and seats, swing out for maintenance while the end pieces stay welded into the line. A two-piece body is lighter and cheaper but the valve comes out of the line to change seats. Weld-end valves need the seats protected from heat during welding.

faqs.q: Where is the forged side entry floating ball valve used?
faqs.a: The listing names high-pressure process and utility lines. It fits small-bore, high-class duty where a trunnion valve would be oversized, such as instrument and sampling headers, steam and condensate utilities and chemical injection lines.

faqs.q: How does the forged side entry floating ball valve differ from the metal seated floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The forged valve has PTFE, RPTFE, PEEK or Devlon soft seats for bubble-tight shut-off up to 200 °C, while the [metal seated floating ball valve](/p/metal-seated-floating-ball-valve) has hardfaced metal seats rated to 450 °C for abrasive and hot service. Choose by fluid cleanliness and temperature.

faqs.q: What is the full jacket jacketed ball valve used for?
faqs.a: It handles fluids that thicken or set when they cool, such as molten sulphur, bitumen, asphalt, heavy fuel oil, wax, resins and polymer melts. A heating jacket surrounds the body and is fed with steam or thermal oil, so the fluid in the valve stays at line temperature and the valve does not freeze shut.

faqs.q: What sizes and class does the jacketed ball valve come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 1/2" to 8" (DN15 to DN200) in ASME Class 150 with RF flanged ends. Jacket connections and face-to-face length vary with size, so the full dimension and weight table and the general arrangement drawing are issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: Steam or thermal oil: which heating medium suits the jacketed ball valve?
faqs.a: Either can be used. The valve has a one-piece full jacket with steam or thermal-oil connections, so tell us the heating medium, its pressure and temperature, and the jacket connection size and type you want, and we match the jacket and body to them.

faqs.q: What pressure class does the jacketed ball valve have?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME Class 150, with shell, backseat and seat tests to API 598. The jacket has its own pressure and temperature limits, set by the heating medium, so give us both the line conditions and the steam or oil conditions when you enquire.

faqs.q: What materials is the jacketed ball valve made from?
faqs.a: The body is offered in carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex. The ball is floating, with soft or metal seats, chosen for the fluid and temperature; molten sulphur and bitumen lines usually need the seat material confirmed against the process temperature.

faqs.q: Which standards and tests apply to the jacketed ball valve?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME B16.34 as the design standard and shell, backseat and seat tests to API 598. Material certificates and the pressure-test record are supplied with each valve, and third-party inspection and extra tests can be added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: How does the jacketed ball valve connect to the line and the heating supply?
faqs.a: The line side is RF flanged, and the jacket has steam or thermal-oil connections that you specify by size and type. Operation is by lever, gear operator or actuator. Jacketed pipe and the valve should be heated by the same circuit so there are no cold spots.

faqs.q: How is the jacketed ball valve installed and kept free of set product?
faqs.a: The one-piece jacket removes cold spots at body joints. Bring the jacket up to temperature before cycling the valve, drain condensate from steam jackets, and keep the heating on whenever the line holds product that can set. Cycle the valve regularly so the seats do not stick.

faqs.q: Which fluids and industries use the jacketed ball valve?
faqs.a: The listing names molten sulphur, bitumen, heavy oil, polymer and resin lines. It is used in refineries, bitumen and asphalt plants, sulphur handling and polymer processing, wherever product must stay hot to flow.

faqs.q: How does the jacketed ball valve differ from the cast floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The jacketed valve adds a heating jacket and is listed only in Class 150 up to NPS 8", while the [cast floating ball valve](/p/cast-floating-ball-valve-iso-17292) has no jacket, reaches NPS 10" and has a published size table. Use the jacketed valve only where the product must be kept hot.

faqs.q: What is the metal seated floating ball valve used for?
faqs.a: It is for lines that destroy soft seats: catalyst, slurries, sand, scale, high-temperature steam and thermal oil. The ball and seats are hardfaced and lapped together, so the valve seals metal to metal and keeps sealing under abrasion and heat.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressure classes does the metal seated floating ball valve come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 1/2" to 8" (DN15 to DN200) in ASME Class 150 to 2500 with flanged or butt-weld ends. The size table lists 86 size and class combinations from 1/2" to 4" with lengths for raised-face, ring-joint and butt-weld ends, plus height and weight.

faqs.q: Why are reduced-bore sizes listed with two sizes on the metal seated ball valve?
faqs.a: A reduced-bore valve has end connections of one size and a bore one size smaller. The table lists the end size first and gives the bore in the port column, so a 1" valve with a 3/4" bore shows both. Full-bore versions are also offered.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature range does the metal seated floating ball valve cover?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME Class 150 to 2500 and -46 °C to 450 °C. Allowable pressure for each class falls as temperature rises under ASME B16.34, so confirm the class against your design temperature; the 450 °C upper limit applies to the hardfaced metal seats, not to every body material.

faqs.q: What are the metal seated floating ball valve's ball, seats and body made from?
faqs.a: The ball and seats are hardfaced with tungsten carbide or chrome carbide coating and lapped as a set. The body is carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex. Tungsten carbide suits abrasive slurry and catalyst; chrome carbide is chosen for high-temperature steam and oil.

faqs.q: What leakage class and tests apply to the metal seated floating ball valve?
faqs.a: Lapped metal seats achieve very low leakage; the class, typically to API 6D or ISO 5208, is stated with the quotation for your size and pressure. The listing gives hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D, with material certificates and the pressure-test record supplied.

faqs.q: What operators and end connections does the metal seated floating ball valve take?
faqs.a: Ends are flanged or butt-weld, and operation is by lever, gear operator, or a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator. The stem is blow-out proof with live-loaded packing. For automated lines see our [actuated valves](/c/actuated-valves) and give the operator torque when you enquire.

faqs.q: How should the metal seated floating ball valve be installed and operated?
faqs.a: Metal seats need more torque than soft seats, so size the operator for the lapped seats and the differential pressure. Flush the line before commissioning, because weld spatter and scale damage lapped seats, and cycle the valve fully rather than throttling with it.

faqs.q: Where is the metal seated floating ball valve used?
faqs.a: The listing names abrasive, slurry, catalyst and high-temperature service. Typical uses are refinery catalyst lines, sand and slurry handling, and steam and thermal-oil lines where soft seats would burn or wear out.

faqs.q: How does the metal seated floating ball valve differ from the forged side entry floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The metal seated valve seals metal to metal with hardfaced seats to 450 °C, while the [forged side entry valve](/p/forged-floating-ball-valve-side-entry) uses PTFE, RPTFE, PEEK or Devlon soft seats to 200 °C and gives bubble-tight shut-off on clean fluids. Both reach Class 2500 in the small sizes.

faqs.q: What is the three-way ball valve with L and T port used for?
faqs.a: It diverts flow between two outlets or brings two inlets together in one valve, replacing two valves and a tee. An L-port ball connects the bottom port to either side, and a T-port ball can connect all three ports or any two of them.

faqs.q: What sizes and classes does the three-way L and T port ball valve come in?
faqs.a: The published range is NPS 1/2" to 4" (DN15 to DN100) in ASME Class 150 and 300 with flanged ends on all three ports. No size table is held on this listing; the general arrangement drawing with port-to-port dimensions is issued with the quotation.

faqs.q: L port or T port: which three-way ball valve do I need?
faqs.a: An L port switches flow from one outlet to the other and can close all ports in one position. A T port can also connect all three ports at once, for mixing or bypass. Decide whether you ever need all three ports open together, because that rules out the L port.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature range does the three-way ball valve cover?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME Class 150 and 300 and a temperature range of -46 °C to 200 °C. Allowable pressure in each class falls as temperature rises under ASME B16.34, so give us the design pressure and temperature to confirm the class and seat material.

faqs.q: What materials is the three-way ball valve made from?
faqs.a: The body is carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy steel or duplex, with a floating ball. The listing does not name a seat material for this valve, so we confirm it against the fluid and temperature when you send the data sheet.

faqs.q: Which standards and tests apply to the three-way L and T port ball valve?
faqs.a: The listing gives ASME B16.34 as the design standard and hydrostatic shell and seat tests to API 6D. Material certificates and the pressure-test record come with the valve, and third-party inspection can be added when the order specifies it.

faqs.q: What operators and connections does the three-way ball valve take?
faqs.a: All three ports are flanged, and operation is by lever, gear operator, or a pneumatic, electric or hydraulic actuator. Say whether the actuator should switch between two positions or three, because the ball position sets the flow path. See our [actuated valves](/c/actuated-valves) for automated options.

faqs.q: How should the three-way ball valve be installed and operated?
faqs.a: Mark which port is the common one and keep the handle position aligned with the flow path. In a diverting duty a floating ball seals toward the downstream seat, so check the pressure direction for each position and avoid dead legs, because fluid can be trapped in the closed branch.

faqs.q: Where is the three-way ball valve with L or T port used?
faqs.a: The listing names diverting, mixing and bypass duty. Typical uses are switching a line between two tanks or two pumps, blending two streams and bypassing a filter or heat exchanger without a second valve.

faqs.q: How does the three-way ball valve differ from the cast floating ball valve?
faqs.a: The three-way valve has three flanged ports and an L or T ball for diverting or mixing, in NPS 1/2" to 4", while the [cast floating ball valve](/p/cast-floating-ball-valve-iso-17292) has two ports for on-off isolation up to NPS 10". Both are Class 150 and 300 with a floating ball.
